The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 19.08.2023.
2.

The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 19.08.2023 at about 12.30 p.m., the petitioner was pillion rider in motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-51-HK-9240 which was ridden by her husband Ibrahim from their house to city via Nagawara-Thanisandra Main Road when they have approached element mall in a slowly and cautiously by observing the traffic rules and regulations with due care and caution, at that time the driver of Car bearing Reg. No. PY-01-B- 8555 came from opposite direction from Nagawara towards thanisandra unmind of the traffic rules and regulation, suddenly took his right turn unmindfull of the petitioner, came in high speed and dashed against the petitioner and caused the accident.
Due to the terrific impact, petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of the body.

Immediately, she was shifted to Image diagnostics Hospital, wherein first aid treatment was given and then shifted to Bowring & Lady Curzon Hospital, Bangalore, wherein she was treated as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical expenses, nourishment and conveyance charges.

The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident she was heal and healthy and aged about 21 years, the petitioner was newly married and she was looking after her family affairs without any aid and she used to wash cloths, clean the house, cook for her family members by which she used to save a sum of Rs.15,000/- p.m.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled and unable to look after the said work.
Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notice, the respondent No.1 remained absent.
Hence, placed exparte.

sentences.text: The respondent No.2 appear through its counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and also denying the rash and negligent driving of the offending Car.

Further,
this respondent admitted the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle and policy was inforce as on the date of accident and liability if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy.
Further, this respondent does not admit that the driver of the offending Car and petitioner motorcycle had valid driving license to drive/ride their respective vehicles at the time of the accident.
He also denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
The petitioner colluding with the owner and police filed the false case.
By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessor framed the following issues are as under:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, she is the victim of the motor vehicle accident caused by the driver of Car bearing Reg. No. PY-01-B-8555 on 19.08.2023 at about 12.30 p.m., Thanisandra, Nagawara main road, near Elements Mall, Bangalore and sustained injuries as pleaded in the petition?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

3 . What order or Award?
5.

In order to prove the case of the petitioner, he has got himself examined as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.16 and examined one Vasanth Kumar as PW.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.17 to Ex.P.19 and also examined Dr. B. Ramesh as PW.3 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.20 and 21 and closed their side.
On the other hand, no evidence is lead on behalf of respondents.

6. Heard arguments of both the sides and perused the materials placed on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under; Issue No.1: In the Affirmative, Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following:

:REASONS:
8. ISSUE No.1: The petitioner has contended that on the above said date, time and place he met with accident and sustained grievous injuries occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle.
9.
The petitioner who is injured in this accident has got examined himself as PW-1 by reiterating the averments made in the petition.
He has produced the documents at Ex.P.1 to 16.

Ex.P.1 is the FIR,
Ex.P2 is the complaint, Ex.P.3 is the charge-sheet, Ex.P.4 is the spot mahazar, Ex.P.5 is the Sketch,

Ex.P.6 are the IMV Report, Ex.P.7 is the Wound certificate, Ex.P.8 is the notice u/s 133 of M. V. Act,

10. On going through the materials, it could be seen that 19.08.2023 at about 12.30 p.m., the petitioner was pillion rider in motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-51-HK-9240 which was ridden by her husband Ibrahim from their house to city via Nagawara-Thanisandra Main Road when they have approached element mall in a slowly and cautiously by observing the traffic rules and regulations with due care and caution, at that time the driver of Car bearing Reg. No. PY- 01-B-8555 came from opposite direction from Nagawara towards thanisandra unmind of the traffic rules and regulation,
suddenly took his right turn unmindfull of the petitioner, came in high speed and dashed against the petitioner and caused the accident.
Due to the terrific impact, petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of the body.
Immediately, she was shifted to Image diagnostics Hospital, wherein first aid treatment was given and then shifted to Bowring & Lady Curzon Hospital, Bangalore, wherein she was treated as inpatient.
Accordingly, the Hennur Traffic Police have registered a case in Cr.No.128/2023.

After completion of the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable U/s 279 and 338 of IPC.
11.
The negligence in common parlance means and simply failure to exercise due care, expected of a reasonable prudent person.
It is a breach of duty and negligence in law ranging from an advertence to shameful disregard of safety of others.
In most instances, it is caused or heedlessness or inadvertence, by which the negligent party is unaware of the results, which may follow from his act.
Negligence is that, a breach of duty or lack of probable care in doing something.
In short, it is want of attention and doing of something, which a prudent and reasonable man would not do.

The burden is upon the petitioner to prove that, the accident occurred due to negligent driving of the driver of Car bearing Reg. No. PY-01-B-8555.
12.

As we know evidence in any Summary Proceedings, "The act of Negligence" will have to be assessed on the basis of broad preponderance of probabilities and degree of proof required is not one of beyond reasonable doubt, as it is insisted in criminal case for "The Negligent Act".
13. The certified copy of the First Information (First information statement/s complaint in common para-lace) lodged before the Hennur Traffic Police has been marked as Ex.P2.
On receiving the First Information, the Station House Officer chose to register a case in Crime No. 128/2023.

The said certified copy of First Information Report (F.I.R.) is marked as Ex.P1.
14.

During the Course of examination-in-chief, he got marked Ex.P1 to 10 are the only documents,
which are to be scrutinized to arrive at conclusion- whether the accident was owing to the negligent manner of driving of driver of offending car.

The Ex.P.4 (spot panchanama) and Ex.P.5 (Sketch),
clearly discloses the place of accident and that the police, after registering the First Information,
held investigation and filed the Ex.P.3, Charge-Sheet against the rider of motorcycle U/s. 279 and 338 of IPC.
The Ex.P.6 i.e., certified copy of the IMV Report discloses that, the accident was not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle in question.

sentences.text: 16. In view of the detailed discussion held above, I am of the opinion that, the petitioner has proved negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle and as such the accident in question had taken place.

By relying on evidence of P.W.1 and the Police records, I am of the considered view that the accident in question took place due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No. PY-01-B-8555.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.
17. ISSUE No.2:

The petitioner in her evidence has specifically deposed that, after the accident she was shifted to Image diagnostics Hospital, wherein first aid treatment was given and then shifted to Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital, wherein she was admitted as inpatient and took treatment.
Petitioner has stated in the petition that, she is undergoing deep mental shock, severe pain and sufferings.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
18. PAIN AND SUFFERING:

In the petition as well as in his evidence PW1 deposed that,
immediately after the accident she was shifted to Image diagnostics Hospital, wherein first aid treatment was given and then shifted to Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital, wherein she was admitted as inpatient from 19.08.2023 to 28.08.2023.
The petitioner has produced the discharge summary marked at Ex.P.14 wherein it is mentioned that the petitioner was admitted in the Bowring & Lady Curzon Hospital, Bangalore for 09 days.

She has produced the wound certificate marked at Ex.P.7, which reveals that, petitioner has sustained swelling tenderness of right leg proximal 1/3 and x-ray shows closed proximal tibia fracture and the doctor has opined that the injuries are grievous in nature.
Hence, it is clear that during the above said period the petitioner suffered lot of pain and inconvenience.
Considering all these aspects this tribunal has granted Rs.50,000/- under the head of pain and suffering.
19. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that she has spent huge amount towards medical expenses.
In support of her plea, she has produced 11 medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.16 to the tune of Rs.5,407/-.
Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and treatment taken by the petitioner, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,407/- towards medical expenses.
20. LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID UP PERIOD:

The petitioner has produced Ex.P.14 Discharge summary issued by Bowring & Lady Curzon Hospital, Bangalore, it reveals that, the petitioner took treatment from the said hospital from 19.08.2023 to 28.08.2023 i.e., for 09 days.
Hence, at least 2 months is required to recover from the accidental injuries.
It is the further contended that, the injured petitioner was house wife and earning Rs.15,000/- per month, in support of her income she has not produced any single document.
Thus, there is no cogent material on record to show actual income of the petitioner at the time of accident in question.
Hence, income of petitioner is to be fixed notionally.
It is pertinent to note that, Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Service Authority framed chart of notional income and directed to follow the same.

As per the said Afra Mehek vs Madan Mohan A on 30 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73016241/
5 guidelines, the fixed notional income for the year 2023 is at Rs.16,000/-.

entities.text: Afra Mehek vs Madan Mohan A on 30 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, 2 months is to be considered as loss of income.
Hence, she is entitled for compensation of Rs.32,000/- under this head.
21. Towards loss of future earning capacity on account of Permanent Physical Disability-

The petitioner to prove her disability, she has produced the evidence of Dr. B. Ramesh in order to substantiate the same, PW.3 who has opined that, total physical disability of 30% and that of whole body disability at 15%.
Admittedly, the PW.3 is not a treated doctor.

Same was admitted by the PW.3 during his cross examination, the relevant evidence of the PW.3 reads as follows :
"It is true to suggest that, I am not a treated doctor."
He was sworn that, petitioner has got 15% disability to the whole body but he was not issued the disability certificate.
It is quite but natural that to help the petitioner doctor will give exaggerated disability.
However, looking to the nature of the injuries it is proper to came to conclusion that there is 10% of disability to the petitioner.
22. Before proceeding on merits of the claim the age of the petitioner /injured has to be determined.
Ex.P.15 is the Aadhar Card of the petitioner, wherein his DOB is mentioned as 11.10.2002 and accident took place in the year 2023.
Accordingly, I assess her age as 21 years at the time of this accident.
As per the ruling reported in AIR 2009 SCW page-3014 between SARLA VERAMA AND OTHERS VS DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND OTHERS, the relevant multiplier applicable is '18'.

entities.text: SARLA VERAMA AND OTHERS VS DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND OTHERS
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Under this head the petitioner is entitled for an amount of Rs.3,45,600/-.
23. FOOD, CONVEYANCE, NOURISHMENT AND ATTENDANT CHARGES:
Further the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took treatment as inpatient in Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital, Bangalore as inpatient from 19.08.2023 to 28.08.2023 i.e., for 09 days.

Hence, she is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/-
under the head of nutritious food and attendant charges.
24. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The petitioner was aged about 21 years at the time of accident, she has sustained grievous injuries.
It shows that she found difficulty in doing day to day works.
She might have suffered lot of pain and loss of amenities and comforts in life.
Therefore, considering the age, nature of injuries and percentage of disability, Rs.20,000/- is awarded under the head of loss of future amenities and happiness.
25. TOWARDS FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES :
The petitioner has claimed towards future medical expenses.
The doctor who has been examined as PW.3 has suggested for removal of the implants and estimate of this surgery will be approximately Rs.10,000/- to Rs.15,000/-.
By keeping nature of the injuries sustained, as he is bound to suffer medical problems in future and cannot every time depend upon Government hospital.
Hence, under this head Rs.10,000/- is awarded.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.4,93,007/- under various heads.
27. LIABILITY:

As discussed in Issue No.1, the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No. PY-01-B-8555 and the police have conducted due enquiry and filed charge sheet against the said driver of the offending vehicle.
From perusal of the policy, the offending vehicle was insured with the respondent No.2 for the period from 31.10.2022 to 30.10.2023.

Admittedly,
the accident in question took place on 19.08.2023.
Hence, policy was in force at the time of accident.
Hence, in view of above discussion, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

However,
respondent No.2 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1 owner.
28. INTEREST:

As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.

sentences.text: By relying on the aforesaid decision, 6% interest awarded to the petitioners in the present case on hand.
Accordingly, issue No.3 is answered partly in the affirmative.
29. ISSUE No.4:

In view of above discussions, I proceed to pass the following:

sentences.text: The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of I.M.V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.4,93,007/- with interest @ 6%
p.a., (excluding the interest on future medical expenses) from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 being insurer of the vehicle involved in an accident is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the above compensation amount with interest thereon before Tribunal within two months from the date of this award.
In the event of deposit of total compensation amount of petitioner, 50% of amount shall be released in his favour along with interest thereon.

Remaining 50% of compensation amount of  petitioner in total compensation amount including interest thereon shall be deposited in his name as F.D. in any of the Nationalized or Scheduled Bank as per choice of petitioner for a period of two years.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon, disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.
2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated:19.08.2019.

The petitioner is hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contains compulsorily photograph of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Adhar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission by the Tribunal.

Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner after expiry of two years period of deposit on proper verification and identification,
without waiting for further order of court.
The advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

Hence, policy was in force at the time of accident.
However,
respondent No.2 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1 owner.
As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.

The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of I.M.V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.4,93,007/- with interest @ 6%
p.a., (excluding the interest on future medical expenses) from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 being insurer of the vehicle involved in an accident is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the above compensation amount with interest thereon before Tribunal within two months from the date of this award.
In the event of deposit of total compensation amount of petitioner, 50% of amount shall be released in his favour along with interest thereon.
Remaining 50% of compensation amount of  petitioner in total compensation amount including interest thereon shall be deposited in his name as F.D. in any of the Nationalized or Scheduled Bank as per choice of petitioner for a period of two years.
After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon, disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.
2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated:19.08.2019.
The petitioner is hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contains compulsorily photograph of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Adhar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission by the Tribunal.
Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner after expiry of two years period of deposit on proper verification and identification,
without waiting for further order of court.
The advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
